blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Transport groups urged six Metro Manila local government units to defer the reimplementation of the Non-Contact Apprehension Policy (NCAP), saying their motion for reconsideration remains pending before the Supreme Court (SC). Transport leaders Boy Vargas of ALTODAP, Obet Martin of Pasang Masda, and Liberty de Luna of ACTO, said the local governments of Manila, Quezon City, Valenzuela, Parañaque, Muntinlupa, and San Juan should await the SC’s final ruling on the legality of the NCAP implementation. The groups said that NCAP violates due process, with some of its provisions being unreasonable, particularly for public utility vehicle operators. “I am […]...
